_comment: Copy to <company-role>.json and edit. Only targetRole is really required. 'experience'/'projects' entries reference names in ../src/data/work.ts (matched case-insensitively, prefix or substring — so 'LiveAgent' or 'NASES' is enough). Bullets live here (the site data is kept terse); this is where each application's tailoring goes. Read the 'Writing the skills section' notes in README.md before filling in 'skills'.
targetRole: The exact job title you're applying for — or a plain one like 'Software Engineer' when the listing's own title is narrower than the pitch
summary: 2-3 sentence pitch tailored to this listing. Omit to use the default summary from src/data/profile.ts.

skills.label: Group by KIND OF TECHNOLOGY, not by tier or by the listing's headings
items: Conventional groups: Languages | Mobile | Frameworks & Libraries | Databases & Messaging | Cloud, DevOps & Tools | AI / ML
Name only things you USE: a library, language, database, service, tool

Never things you DO: 'REST API design', 'Push notifications', 'Play Store releases', 'Real-time data pipelines', 'Incident response', 'Domain-Driven Design' — those go in experience bullets, attached to a product
Prefer the specific artefact over the activity: 'Firebase Cloud Messaging' not 'Push notifications'
Drop a language or tool the listing has no use for, and drop it from the summary prose too so the two agree

projects: work.ts entry names for the compact Selected Projects strip. Omit for none.
_emphasize_note: OFF BY DEFAULT — leave 'emphasize' out. Accent-highlighting the exact chips a listing asks for tells the reader the CV was built for that one advert. Only use it when a CV is not going to a recruiter who will see another version. To use it: "emphasize": ["Kotlin", "FastAPI"] — strings must match a skills item exactly (case-insensitive); matched items also sort to the front of their group.
_skillGroups_note: Alternative to 'skills': "skillGroups": ["Platform & Cloud-Native", "Product & Architecture", "Applied AI / ML"] reuses the site's own pillars from src/i18n/ui.ts verbatim, in that order. Omit both for all pillars. Custom 'skills' wins when both are set.
